title: kitbash.yaml
description: The one manifest. A folder with name and description is visible knowledge. A folder that also carries deploy is a Package.

name.description: Lowercase kebab-case identifier, unique within its parent folder. Doubles as the tool namespace when the Package is exposed over MCP.

description.description: One or two sentences an agent reads to decide whether to enter this folder or use this Package. Say what it is and when to use it.

tags.description: Free text labels for humans to search by. Platform logic never reads tags.

provides.description: What this folder offers. Every block is optional. A Package with no provides block is a batch job or a subscriber.

tools.description: Tools this Package exposes. Composition binds on their schemas, never on names or tags.

prompt.description: Relative path to a file an agent should read before using the tools. Markdown by convention.

subscriptions.description: Streams this Package wants delivered. Only telemetry exists today.

kit.description: Lifecycle hooks this Package implements. Presence makes it a kit.

deploy.description: How this folder runs. Presence makes the folder a Package.

units.description: A Package runs as one Process. More than one unit runs as one pod, at most eight of them: every unit is a container, an environment file and a mount check of one start, see PLAN.md section 5.6.

permits.description: What a Process of this Package may call over /mcp. A Process with no permits block gets an empty surface: the block is the declaration, not a filter on top of one. It narrows nothing for a member's own SSH session.

tools.description: Surface tool names this Package may call, as globs, plus the reserved word packages. A * matches any run of characters within a name, so fs_* is the fs family; a glob matches whatever it matches, built in tools included, because writing one is declaring them. The word packages stands for every tool the owner's running Processes publish and for no built in, which is what a kit that composes other kits needs. A tool that matches nothing here is not published to the Process and calling it is not-permitted.

paths.description: Absolute Files path prefixes this Package may name. A prefix covers the path itself and everything below it, and a * stands for exactly one whole component, so /home/*/flows is that folder in every member's home. A Process with tools but no paths may call nothing that takes a path.

name.description: Tool name within the Package namespace, exactly as the server names it. MCP allows letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. Exposed to agents as <package>_<name>; package names carry no underscore, so the first underscore is the split.

schemaRef.description: Either an inline JSON Schema 2020-12 object or a $ref to a schema file inside this folder.

name.description: What this unit is called inside its Package. It is required when a Package declares more than one unit and unique among them, because a unit that is one of several is named by proc_logs and by proc_list and stamped on its own Telemetry records. A single unit may omit it and is the Package itself. See PLAN.md section 5.6.

build.description: Relative path to a build context inside this folder. Mutually exclusive with image.

image.description: An existing OCI image reference pinned by digest. Mutually exclusive with build.

builder.description: Absolute path of a Package folder whose manifest declares provides.kit: [build] and a tool build with input {path, context}. pkg_build calls that kit instead of the built in OCI path; without this field the built in path builds the unit. The kit has to be running as a Process of the caller. A builder is paired with a runner in practice: the image it builds is in that kit's hands rather than in this member's image store, so the unit usually names the kit that runs it as well.

runner.description: Absolute path of a Package folder whose manifest declares provides.kit: [run] and a tool run with input {package, digest, name, unit}. proc_run calls that kit instead of the built in rootless podman runner, and the kit owns the Process it answers with: kitbashd registers it, does not supervise it and does not restore it at boot. The kit has to be running as a Process of the caller.

expose.description: mcp: tools appear on the caller's MCP surface. http: an internal port, optionally a hostname. none: no ingress.

port.description: Container port to expose when expose is http or mcp.

hostname.description: One host name kitbashd serves this Process under, in place of the <name>.<member>.<domain> it derives. A lower case DNS name of at least two labels, outside KITBASH_DOMAIN and never an address, whose record points at this host: kitbashd resolves it at proc_run and at every start and serves it only while it answers with an address of this host or is a CNAME to the derived name. A name under the host domain or an address is invalid-manifest, a name another Process on this host already serves is conflict, and a name that does not point here is not-permitted. It is served only when the host has a domain; without one an http Process keeps its internal port and nothing is routed. See PLAN.md section 2.3.

schedule.description: Five cron fields, minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, read in UTC. A unit that declares one is a job: proc_run registers it and starts nothing, kitbashd starts the container at each tick as the owner and the run is over when the entrypoint exits, and every run writes one kitbash.schedule metric record. The dialect is *, a number, a range a-b, a step */s or a-b/s and comma separated lists of those; names are not accepted, a signed number is not, the whole expression is one line, and day of week takes 0 to 7 with both 0 and 7 meaning Sunday. When both day fields are restricted a day matches if either does, and a day field beginning with * is not a restriction whatever step follows it, so "0 9 */2 * 1" is Mondays and nothing else, which is what every other cron does. It is allowed only with expose: none and without health, restart or provides.subscriptions, each of which describes a Process that stays up; any of them beside a schedule is invalid-manifest. A tick that arrives while the previous run is still going is skipped and recorded, ticks missed while the host was down are not made up, and a run longer than six hours is stopped. See PLAN.md section 2.3.

environment.description: Plain environment variables, written into the container as the manifest spells them, the map form compose spells the same way. A credential belongs in secrets instead, because everything here is readable by anyone who can read the manifest.

command.description: The command the container runs, in place of the CMD of its image, as compose spells it. It is a list of arguments and not a shell line: the words are passed to the image's entrypoint as they are written. A credential belongs in secrets instead, because these words go on podman's command line, where anyone on the host reads them in ps and the container runtime keeps them with the container. A unit that wants the image's own command declares none.

secrets.description: Environment variable names this unit needs and does not get from the image, from environment or from kitbashd: an API key, a token for a service outside this machine. Names only. The member sets the value with secrets_set, kitbashd keeps it as a root owned file outside the database, and every start resolves each name to the owner's current value and writes it into the environment file the container is created with, so a value never crosses a request body or a command line. A name environment also sets, and a name kitbashd speaks for, which is every KITBASH_ name, are both invalid-manifest. A declared name the member has not set is not-found at proc_run. See PLAN.md section 2.3.

items.description: An environment variable name in the spelling a credential is written in.

health.description: How a Process is probed. kitbashd requests http on the Process's endpoint every interval and records the answer as the metric kitbash.health; it restarts nothing. exec is recorded and run by nobody.

http.description: Path probed on port, for expose: http and expose: mcp. Probed only when the Process publishes an endpoint.

interval.description: How often the path is requested. An interval under 5s is raised to 5s.

mounts.description: Folders of Files this unit sees as bind mounts, at most four. source is a folder under the owner's own home or a top level folder of /org, and it has to be visible by the rule the fs family reads by: it, or a folder between it and its root, carries a kitbash.yaml with a name and a description, so the folders inside a Package are mountable and a folder with no manifest anywhere above it is not. target is where the container sees it, and may not be / or land under /proc, /sys, /dev, /etc, /bin, /sbin, /usr, /lib or /lib64. mode rw is allowed only under the owner's home; /org is read only for everyone, admins included, because an approval is the way a member writes there. kitbashd resolves every source as root at registration and again at every start, so a mount that stops being legal fails the start rather than being carried over, and it reads the container back once it exists, so a source replaced while podman was resolving it fails the start and the container is removed. Mounts are independent of provides.permits: a permit governs what a Process may call over /mcp, a mount is a kernel fact. See PLAN.md section 2.3.

source.description: Absolute path of the folder to mount, under /home/<owner> or /org.

target.description: Absolute path the container sees it at. Not / and nothing under /proc, /sys, /dev, /etc, /bin, /sbin, /usr, /lib or /lib64.

mode.description: ro mounts the folder read only, rw read write. rw is refused outside the owner's own home.

filesUnit.description: Files placed somewhere at deploy time. Reserved; not implemented in version 1.
